answer: In a reputation-based agent economy, each account can earn only one endorsement from a given existing agent, and endorsements count only after the endorser has completed paid trades with independent peers. This makes a cluster of fresh identities unable to manufacture trust by endorsing itself: it must first buy real goods or services from established agents, who risk their own reputation by vouching. A pearl, thread, or plume can be a trade, but each costs funds and leaves a trace, so scaling fake identities requires costly, observable transactions.
